source.title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems

accepted.question_text: Classify Riemannian geodesic-orbit manifolds in the dimensions where no complete classification is known. A Riemannian homogeneous manifold M=G/K with metric g is a geodesic-orbit, or g.o., manifold when every geodesic is homogeneous with respect to the largest connected isometry group, meaning that each geodesic through the origin o can be written as gamma(t)=exp(tX).o for some nonzero X in the Lie algebra of G. What is a complete classification of such g.o. manifolds, especially in dimension 7 and in dimensions greater than 7?

For a fixed Riemannian homogeneous space M=G/K and a fixed connected transitive isometry group G, determine all G-invariant Riemannian metrics g for which (M=G/K,g) is a G-g.o. space. In this setting, G-g.o. means that every geodesic is an orbit gamma(t)=exp(tX).o of a one-parameter subgroup of G. Can the classification of all such metrics be carried out for arbitrary homogeneous spaces rather than only for known families?

For a homogeneous Riemannian space (M=G/K,g) that is not a g.o. space, explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics it does have. Equivalently, determine which nonzero vectors X in the Lie algebra of G make gamma(t)=exp(tX).o a geodesic, and give an effective method for computing these geodesic vectors even when not every geodesic of M is homogeneous.

Classify g.o. spaces whose isotropy representation decomposes into two or three irreducible isotropy summands. Here M=G/K is a homogeneous space, m=T_o(G/K) is the tangent module at the origin, and the isotropy representation of K on m splits as a direct sum of two or three irreducible submodules; the task is to determine exactly which invariant metrics on such spaces make every geodesic an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup.

evidence.quote: two or three irreducible isotropy summands

accepted.question_text: Give criteria or proofs determining when the g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric is independent of the chosen coset representation M=G/K and of the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g=k+m. Equivalently, clarify when the assertion that (M=G/K,g) is G-g.o. remains valid, changes, or must be reformulated after representing the same Riemannian manifold by another transitive isometry group or another reductive complement.

evidence.quote: does not depend on the representation

accepted.question_text: Extend key Riemannian criteria for homogeneous geodesics to pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds. In particular, formulate pseudo-Riemannian analogues of algebraic tests for when one-parameter curves gamma(t)=exp(t(a+x)).o are geodesics and for when multi-exponential curves gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)exp(tZ).o are geodesics, while accounting for the pseudo-Riemannian possibility that a homogeneous null geodesic has a non-affine parameter.

Decide whether every search for homogeneous geodesics represented by three or more exponential factors can be reduced to a search for two-step homogeneous geodesics. A two-step homogeneous geodesic is a geodesic through o of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o with X and Y in the Lie algebra of G, and a two-step g.o. space is a homogeneous space in which every geodesic through the origin has such a representation.

Develop the theory of two-step homogeneous geodesics in pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds, including a pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma that characterizes when a curve of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o is a geodesic.

For generalized Wallach spaces of type 2 or type 3 with invariant metrics determined by positive parameters (lambda_1,lambda_2,lambda_3), where at least two parameters are different, determine all homogeneous geodesics by solving or otherwise characterizing the system of dim(m_1)+dim(m_2)+dim(m_3) quadratic equations for geodesic vectors. A generalized Wallach space is a compact homogeneous space G/K whose tangent module m decomposes as m_1+m_2+m_3 into three Ad(K)-invariant irreducible modules that are pairwise orthogonal with respect to the negative Killing form and satisfy [m_i,m_i] contained in k.
